name: Cubic Addressing Scheme
definition: A memory addressing scheme where the basic unit for address calculation is an s^3 sub-cube instead of a single voxel. Voxels are grouped into sub-cubes that fit into a row of an SDRAM.
summary: The Cubic Addressing Scheme optimizes dense volume rendering by grouping voxels into sub-cubes to align with SDRAM row access patterns, reducing cache refreshes compared to traditional linear addressing.
